title: Trigonometric Functions
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: General solutions when trig functions equal zero?
cards.a:
sin θ = 0 ⇒ θ = nπ
cos θ = 0 ⇒ θ = (2n + 1)π/2
tan θ = 0 ⇒ θ = nπ  (where n ∈ Z).
cards.hint: Zeros of tan θ coincide with zeros of sin θ.

cards.q: General solutions of sin θ = sin α, cos θ = cos α, tan θ = tan α?
cards.a:
sin θ = sin α ⇒ θ = nπ + (-1)ⁿ α
cos θ = cos α ⇒ θ = 2nπ ± α
tan θ = tan α ⇒ θ = nπ + α  (where n ∈ Z).
cards.hint: Choose α as the principal value of smallest numerical magnitude.

cards.q: General solution for squared trig equations: sin² θ = sin² α, cos² θ = cos² α, tan² θ = tan² α?
cards.a: θ = nπ ± α  (where n ∈ Z) for all three forms.
cards.hint: All three squared equations share the exact same general solution!

cards.q: What is the principal solution of a trigonometric equation?
cards.a: A solution θ that satisfies 0 ≤ θ < 2π.
cards.hint: Every standard trig equation has exactly two principal solutions in [0, 2π).

cards.q: Conversion between Cartesian (x, y) and Polar (r, θ) coordinates?
cards.a:
Cartesian to Polar: r = √(x² + y²), tan θ = y/x (adjust θ for the quadrant of (x, y)).
Polar to Cartesian: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ.
cards.hint: Check signs of x and y to place θ in the correct quadrant (0 ≤ θ < 2π).

cards.q: State the Sine Rule for any triangle ABC.
cards.a: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R = k, where R is the circumradius.
cards.hint: Useful forms: a = 2R sin A, b = 2R sin B, c = 2R sin C.

cards.q: State the Cosine Rule for sides and angles of triangle ABC.
cards.a:
a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A ⇒ cos A = (b² + c² - a²) / (2bc)
b² = c² + a² - 2ca cos B ⇒ cos B = (c² + a² - b²) / (2ca)
c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C ⇒ cos C = (a² + b² - c²) / (2ab).
cards.hint: Denominator has the two sides adjacent to the angle being computed.

cards.q: State the Projection Rules in triangle ABC.
cards.a:
a = b cos C + c cos B
b = c cos A + a cos C
c = a cos B + b cos A.
cards.hint: Each side is the sum of projections of the other two sides onto it.

cards.q: State Napier's Analogies (Tangent Rule).
cards.hint: Notice (b - c) matches angle (B - C) and cot(A/2) uses the third angle.

cards.q: Half-angle formulas for sin(A/2), cos(A/2), and tan(A/2) (s = semi-perimeter)?
cards.hint: sin uses opposite factors (s - b)(s - c); cos uses adjacent factor s(s - a).

cards.q: Formulas for the Area of Triangle (Δ)?
cards.a:
Δ = (1/2) ab sin C = (1/2) bc sin A = (1/2) ca sin B
Δ = abc / (4R) = r · s = √[ s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c) ] (Heron's Formula).
cards.hint: R = circumradius, r = inradius = Δ/s.

cards.q: Principal value branches (Range) of sin⁻¹ x, cos⁻¹ x, and tan⁻¹ x?
cards.a:
sin⁻¹ x: [-π/2, π/2], Domain: [-1, 1]
cos⁻¹ x: [0, π], Domain: [-1, 1]
tan⁻¹ x: (-π/2, π/2), Domain: R.
cards.hint: HSC Board gold mine: always verify if the angle lies inside the principal branch!

cards.q: Principal value branches (Range) of cosec⁻¹ x, sec⁻¹ x, and cot⁻¹ x?
cards.hint: Domains: sec⁻¹ x and cosec⁻¹ x are defined for |x| ≥ 1; cot⁻¹ x for R.

cards.q: Negative argument identities for sin⁻¹, tan⁻¹, cosec⁻¹?
cards.a:
sin⁻¹(-x) = -sin⁻¹(x)
tan⁻¹(-x) = -tan⁻¹(x)
cosec⁻¹(-x) = -cosec⁻¹(x).
cards.hint: These three odd functions push the minus sign directly outside.

cards.q: Negative argument identities for cos⁻¹, sec⁻¹, cot⁻¹?
cards.a:
cos⁻¹(-x) = π - cos⁻¹(x)
sec⁻¹(-x) = π - sec⁻¹(x)
cot⁻¹(-x) = π - cot⁻¹(x).
cards.hint: Super high-yield trap! Never write cos⁻¹(-x) = -cos⁻¹(x). It is ALWAYS π - cos⁻¹(x).

cards.q: Complementary angle identities for inverse trig functions?
cards.a:
sin⁻¹ x + cos⁻¹ x = π/2  (for x ∈ [-1, 1])
tan⁻¹ x + cot⁻¹ x = π/2  (for x ∈ R)
sec⁻¹ x + cosec⁻¹ x = π/2  (for |x| ≥ 1).
cards.hint: Frequently used to substitute π/2 - sin⁻¹ x in place of cos⁻¹ x.

cards.q: Addition formula: tan⁻¹ x + tan⁻¹ y?
cards.a:
If xy < 1: tan⁻¹((x + y) / (1 - xy))
If xy > 1 (x > 0, y > 0): π + tan⁻¹((x + y) / (1 - xy)).
cards.hint: Check the product xy first! If xy > 1, you MUST add π to avoid domain violation.

cards.q: Subtraction formula: tan⁻¹ x - tan⁻¹ y?
cards.a: tan⁻¹ x - tan⁻¹ y = tan⁻¹((x - y) / (1 + xy)), provided xy > -1.
cards.hint: If xy < -1 and x > 0, y < 0, add π.

cards.q: Three standard formulas for 2 tan⁻¹ x?
cards.a: 2 tan⁻¹ x = tan⁻¹(2x / (1 - x²)) = sin⁻¹(2x / (1 + x²)) = cos⁻¹((1 - x²) / (1 + x²)).
cards.hint: Core substitution: put x = tan θ to simplify rational expressions in calculus.

cards.q: Trap: Value of sin⁻¹(sin(2π/3)) and cos⁻¹(cos(4π/3))?
cards.a:
sin⁻¹(sin(2π/3)) = sin⁻¹(sin(π - π/3)) = π/3 (since π/3 ∈ [-π/2, π/2]).
cos⁻¹(cos(4π/3)) = cos⁻¹(cos(2π - 2π/3)) = 2π/3 (since 2π/3 ∈ [0, π]).
cards.hint: Never write 2π/3 or 4π/3! Both fall outside the principal branch.

cards.q: Reciprocal relations for inverse trigonometric functions?
cards.a:
cosec⁻¹ x = sin⁻¹(1/x)  (for |x| ≥ 1)
sec⁻¹ x = cos⁻¹(1/x)  (for |x| ≥ 1)
cot⁻¹ x = tan⁻¹(1/x)  (for x > 0), and π + tan⁻¹(1/x) (for x < 0).
cards.hint: Trap: cot⁻¹(-1) = 3π/4, whereas tan⁻¹(-1) = -π/4. For x < 0, cot⁻¹ x = π + tan⁻¹(1/x).

cards.q: MHT-CET condition for a cos θ + b sin θ = c to have real solutions?
cards.a: Real solutions exist if and only if c² ≤ a² + b² (i.e. -√(a² + b²) ≤ c ≤ √(a² + b²)).
cards.hint: Maximum value of a cos θ + b sin θ is √(a² + b²); minimum is -√(a² + b²).

cards.q: In any triangle ABC (A + B + C = π), what is tan A + tan B + tan C?
cards.a: tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A · tan B · tan C.
cards.hint: Likewise: cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = cot(A/2) · cot(B/2) · cot(C/2).

cards.q: If in ΔABC, a² + b² = c², what are the angles and circumradius R?
cards.a: Angle C = 90° (right triangle). Circumradius R = c/2 (hypotenuse / 2).
cards.hint: By Sine Rule: c / sin 90° = 2R ⇒ R = c/2.

cards.q: Shortcut to evaluate tan( (1/2) cos⁻¹(a/b) ) + tan( (1/2) cos⁻¹(-a/b) )?
cards.a: Value is 2b / a.
cards.hint: Put (1/2) cos⁻¹(a/b) = θ ⇒ cos 2θ = a/b, then tan θ + tan(π/2 - θ) = tan θ + cot θ = 2 / sin 2θ.
